Karnes and Weinrib are hired for summer 1952 to take over Turner's duties and supervise the Pottery Seminar planned for October. Weinrib quickly explores the sculptural possibilities of slab-built pieces and tiles, decorated with brushstrokes, molded elements, or incised patterns in response to the art of his new surroundings. Karnes continues making functional pottery: simple forms whose surface rings show the process, pieces for sale and used in the college dining hall.
